## Teaching points

1. Syncope can be the only symptom of PE; normal oxygen saturation and no dyspnea do not exclude it.
2. Syncope plus hypotension calls for bedside echocardiography: a dilated RV with paradoxical septal motion in shock means obstructive shock until proven otherwise.
3. High-risk PE (2019 ESC) is cardiac arrest, obstructive shock or persistent hypotension; start unfractionated heparin with a weight-adjusted bolus as soon as it is suspected.
4. Confirm with CTPA when it is immediately available and the patient can travel; if not, RV dysfunction on echo justifies reperfusion therapy.
5. Systemic thrombolysis is first-line for high-risk PE without contraindications; surgical embolectomy or catheter-directed therapy if lysis is contraindicated or fails.
